note.explanation: Environmental chemistry studies how human activities and natural processes affect the environment. Air pollutants can harm health, plants, animals and climate. Pollution can be reduced by cleaner energy, responsible choices and environmental protection.
examples: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a poisonous pollutant produced by incomplete fuel combustion.
Sulphur and nitrogen oxides can react with water in the atmosphere to form acid rain.
note.checkAnswer: Examples include carbon monoxide, sulphur oxides and nitrogen oxides.
note.simple: Some gases and particles in the air harm living things. Understanding their sources and effects helps us protect people and the environment.
note.checkQuestion: Name one pollutant gas that can contribute to acid rain.
note.title: Environmental chemistry: air pollution and its effects
steps: Identify the pollutant and its source.
Explain how it affects people, plants, animals or climate.
Give a practical way to reduce it.
note.answer: Sulphur dioxide is one pollutant gas that can contribute to acid rain.

mcqs.stem: Q10.1. Which gases are responsible for greenhouse effect?
rationales: These gases are not the pair identified as responsible for the greenhouse effect in this question.
This pair is not the correct greenhouse-gas pair given in the options.
Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases, so this is correct.
Oxygen and nitrogen are not the greenhouse-gas pair sought here.

options: Waste gases from digestion of animals
mcqs.stem: Q10.2. Indicate the source of sulphur which is responsible for the presence of oxides of sulphur in the atmosphere.
rationales: This is not the principal source of atmospheric sulphur oxides in this question.
Animal digestion gases are not the source identified here.
Photochemical smog is not the source of the sulphur in sulphur oxides.
Burning sulphur-containing fossil fuels releases sulphur oxides, so this is correct.

mcqs.stem: Q10.3. Concentration of which gas in the atmosphere is decreased by photosynthesis in plants?
rationales: Photosynthesis releases oxygen rather than decreasing its concentration.
Photosynthesis does not use atmospheric nitrogen as its carbon source.
Plants take in carbon dioxide during photosynthesis, so this is correct.
Water vapour is not the gas used by plants as the carbon source in photosynthesis.

mcqs.stem: Q10.4. Which substance remains unaffected in the catalytic converter fixed in the exhaust of the automobiles?
rationales: Carbon dioxide is not changed by the catalytic converter, so this is correct.
The converter oxidises carbon monoxide to carbon dioxide.
Nitric oxide is converted by the converter into nitrogen-containing products.
Nitrogen dioxide is not the unaffected substance intended here.

mcqs.stem: Q10.5. People of which age groups are most affected by the air pollution?
rationales: Young adults are not the two especially vulnerable age groups in the answer.
Middle-aged people are not the two especially vulnerable age groups in the answer.
Children are particularly vulnerable, but the option does not include the other high-risk group.
Children and aged people are both especially vulnerable, so this is correct.

mcqs.stem: Q10.6. In which area there is a greater possibility of acid rain?
rationales: Villages generally have fewer concentrated emissions of acid-rain-forming gases.
Big cities can have air pollution, but the best answer here is the area with concentrated industrial emissions.
Industries release sulphur and nitrogen oxides that can form acid rain, so this is correct.
Water bodies are not the main emission source that makes acid rain more likely.

options: Because fog is not present in summer
Because due to heat of the Earth the smoke rises up
Because in summer smoke and fog cannot mix with each other
Because less fossil fuels are burnt in summer
mcqs.stem: Q10.7. Why is smog not felt in summer?
rationales: Fog is less common in summer, but this is not the explanation given by the correct choice.
Heat makes smoke rise and disperse, so this is correct.
Smoke and fog can mix; summer heat does not prevent their mixing in this way.
This does not explain the seasonal dispersal of smoke.

mcqs.stem: Q10.8. Which catalyst is used in the catalytic converter fixed in the exhaust systems of automobiles?
rationales: Nickel is not the set of catalysts specified for automobile catalytic converters here.
Copper is not the set of catalysts specified for automobile catalytic converters here.
Platinum, palladium and rhodium are the catalysts used, so this is correct.
Calcium oxide is not the catalyst set used in these converters.

mcqs.stem: Q10.9. Which components are essential for the formation of photochemical smog?
rationales: This set does not contain the required volatile organic compounds and sunlight together.
Nitrogen dioxide, volatile organic compounds and sunlight are essential components, so this is correct.
This set lacks volatile organic compounds.
This set lacks sunlight, which is needed for photochemical reactions.

options: Both the oxides of nitrogen and sulfur
mcqs.stem: Q10.10. Which gases contribute towards the formation of acid rain?
rationales: Carbon oxides are not the gases identified as the main acid-rain contributors here.
Sulphur oxides contribute, but this option leaves out nitrogen oxides.
Nitrogen oxides contribute, but this option leaves out sulphur oxides.
Both sulphur and nitrogen oxides contribute to acid rain, so this is correct.

written.text: Q10.1. What is the main objective of environmental education?
written.finalAnswer: To create awareness and understanding of environmental problems and encourage people to protect the environment.

rubric.why: The answer must state the central purpose of environmental education.
rubric.description: States that it creates environmental awareness or understanding.
rubric.how: Mention awareness and understanding of the environment or its problems.

rubric.why: The purpose includes guiding people towards responsible action.
rubric.description: Connects this awareness with solving problems or protecting the environment.
rubric.how: State that awareness should lead to environmental protection or problem-solving.

modelAnswer: Environmental education creates awareness and understanding of environmental problems.
It encourages people to take responsible steps to protect the environment.

written.text: Q10.2. How is particulate matter released in the atmosphere?
written.finalAnswer: It is released as tiny solid particles and liquid droplets from sources such as fuel combustion, industries, vehicles and dust.

rubric.why: Particulate matter consists of small particles or droplets suspended in air.
rubric.description: Identifies particulate matter as tiny particles or droplets.
rubric.how: Describe its physical form.

rubric.why: Naming sources explains how it enters the atmosphere.
rubric.description: Gives at least one suitable source.
rubric.how: Name fuel burning, industry, vehicles or dust.

modelAnswer: Particulate matter is released into air as tiny solid particles and liquid droplets.
Sources include fuel combustion, industries, vehicles and dust.

written.text: Q10.3. Which gas is more poisonous, CO₂ or CO?
written.finalAnswer: CO

rubric.why: The answer distinguishes highly poisonous carbon monoxide from carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: Correctly identifies carbon monoxide.
rubric.how: Write CO or carbon monoxide.

modelAnswer: CO is more poisonous than CO₂.

written.text: Q10.4. How does acid rain affect forests?
written.finalAnswer: Acid rain damages leaves and trees, reduces soil fertility and can harm forest growth.

rubric.why: Damage to trees and leaves is a direct effect on forests.
rubric.description: States that acid rain damages forest plants or leaves.
rubric.how: Describe harm to leaves, trees or their growth.

rubric.why: Acid rain can also affect the soil on which forests depend.
rubric.description: States another effect such as reduced soil fertility or poor growth.
rubric.how: Mention a soil or forest-growth effect.

modelAnswer: Acid rain damages the leaves and trees of forests.
It can reduce soil fertility and hinder forest growth.

written.text: Q10.5. In what way sulphur present in fossil fuels becomes dangerous?
written.finalAnswer: When fossil fuels are burnt, their sulphur forms sulphur oxides, which pollute the air and can produce acid rain.

rubric.why: Burning releases the sulphur compounds into the air.
rubric.description: Explains that danger arises when sulphur-containing fuels are burnt.
rubric.how: Link sulphur to fossil-fuel combustion.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the harmful products or effect.
rubric.description: Names sulphur oxides and/or the resulting acid rain.
rubric.how: State that sulphur oxides pollute air and contribute to acid rain.

modelAnswer: When fossil fuels containing sulphur are burnt, sulphur combines with oxygen to form oxides of sulphur.
These oxides pollute the air and can cause acid rain.

written.text: Q10.6. Name any three major sources responsible for the greenhouse effect.
written.finalAnswer: Burning fossil fuels, deforestation and emissions from industries and vehicles.

rubric.why: Fossil-fuel burning releases greenhouse gases.
rubric.description: Names one valid source.
rubric.how: Give a source such as fossil-fuel burning.

rubric.why: The question requests three sources, so more than one source is needed.
rubric.description: Names two further valid sources; any three suitable sources earn full credit.
rubric.how: Include deforestation, industrial emissions or vehicle emissions.

modelAnswer: Three major sources are burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and emissions from industries and vehicles.

written.text: Q10.7. How is wind energy useful for us?
written.finalAnswer: Wind energy can generate electricity and can be used to operate windmills for pumping water or grinding grain.

rubric.why: Electricity generation is a major practical use of wind energy.
rubric.description: Names electricity generation.
rubric.how: State that wind turbines generate electricity.

rubric.why: A second useful application completes the answer.
rubric.description: Names another use such as pumping water or grinding grain.
rubric.how: Give one other practical use.

modelAnswer: Wind energy is used to generate electricity.
It can also operate windmills for pumping water or grinding grain.

written.text: Q10.1. How is the excessive use of insecticides and pesticides harmful for birds?
written.finalAnswer: Birds may eat contaminated insects or seeds; pesticides can accumulate in their bodies, poison them and reduce their reproduction and populations.

rubric.why: The answer must explain how birds are exposed to these chemicals.
rubric.description: Explains that birds consume contaminated food or are exposed to pesticides.
rubric.how: Link pesticide use to contaminated insects, seeds or food.

rubric.why: Accumulation explains why repeated exposure is dangerous.
rubric.description: Explains that pesticides can accumulate in birds or along food chains.
rubric.how: Mention accumulation or bioaccumulation.

rubric.why: Reproductive harm is an important biological effect.
rubric.description: Mentions reduced reproduction, egg damage or breeding failure.
rubric.how: State one reproductive effect.

rubric.why: The consequences for survival and bird populations complete the explanation.
rubric.description: States poisoning, death or a decline in bird numbers.
rubric.how: Give a harmful outcome for birds.

modelAnswer: Birds may eat insects or seeds contaminated with insecticides and pesticides.
These chemicals can accumulate in their bodies through the food chain.
They may poison birds and interfere with reproduction, including successful egg production and hatching.
As a result, bird numbers may decline.

written.text: Q10.2. Percentage of CO₂ in air is only 0.04%. Then how does it become harmful for the ecosystem?
written.finalAnswer: Although its percentage is small, CO₂ traps outgoing heat; increased CO₂ strengthens the greenhouse effect, causing global warming and climate change that disturb ecosystems.

rubric.why: Recognising the small percentage addresses the question's premise.
rubric.description: Acknowledges that CO₂ is present in a small proportion of air.
rubric.how: Refer to its low concentration or the stated percentage.

rubric.why: The heat-trapping property explains why a small quantity still matters.
rubric.description: Explains CO₂'s role in the greenhouse effect.
rubric.how: State that CO₂ traps outgoing heat.

rubric.why: This identifies the consequence of increased greenhouse effect.
rubric.description: Links higher CO₂ with warming or climate change.
rubric.how: State the warming consequence.

rubric.why: The answer must connect climate effects to ecosystem harm.
rubric.description: Gives an ecosystem consequence.
rubric.how: Mention disrupted habitats, species or environmental conditions.

modelAnswer: Although CO₂ makes up only about 0.04% of air, it absorbs and traps some outgoing heat.
When its concentration increases, the greenhouse effect becomes stronger.
This causes global warming and climate change.
Changes in temperature, rainfall and habitats can disturb ecosystems and harm organisms.

written.text: Q10.3. Why only some pollutant gases present in the atmosphere cause green house effect while others do not?
written.finalAnswer: Only gases that absorb outgoing infrared radiation and retain heat contribute significantly to the greenhouse effect; gases that do not absorb it do not have this effect.

rubric.why: The answer must distinguish gases by their properties rather than simply their presence in air.
rubric.description: States that the effect depends on the type of gas.
rubric.how: Make clear that not every atmospheric gas behaves alike.

rubric.why: Absorbing outgoing heat radiation is the key scientific explanation.
rubric.description: Explains that greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared heat radiation.
rubric.how: Name the radiation and explain its absorption or retention.

rubric.why: This connects the gas property to warming.
rubric.description: States that absorbed heat is retained and contributes to the effect.
rubric.how: Link absorption to trapping heat.

modelAnswer: Only some pollutant gases absorb the outgoing infrared radiation from Earth.
They retain some of this heat in the atmosphere and therefore contribute to the greenhouse effect.
Other gases that do not absorb this radiation do not significantly cause this effect.

written.text: Q10.4. How can you reduce the emission of CO present in the gases emitted by the burning of fuel in the automobile engines?
written.finalAnswer: Use a catalytic converter in the exhaust system; it oxidises CO to CO₂. Proper engine maintenance and complete fuel combustion also reduce CO emissions.

rubric.why: The converter is the main control method asked for in the chapter.
rubric.description: Names a catalytic converter fitted to the automobile exhaust.
rubric.how: State the device used to control exhaust CO.

rubric.why: Explaining the conversion shows how the device reduces poisonous CO.
rubric.description: Explains that CO is oxidised to CO₂.
rubric.how: Write the conversion of carbon monoxide to carbon dioxide.

rubric.why: An additional practical measure strengthens the response.
rubric.description: Adds proper engine maintenance or complete combustion.
rubric.how: Mention one supplementary way to reduce CO formation.

modelAnswer: A catalytic converter can be fitted in the exhaust system of an automobile.
It oxidises poisonous CO to CO₂.
Keeping the engine properly maintained and ensuring more complete combustion also reduces CO emissions.

written.text: Q10.5. Mention three different ways in which solar energy can be useful for us.
written.finalAnswer: Solar energy can be used for heating water, cooking food and generating electricity.

rubric.why: One correctly described application earns the first mark.
rubric.description: Gives a valid use of solar energy.
rubric.how: Name solar water heating or another valid use.

rubric.why: A second distinct use is required.
rubric.description: Gives a different valid use.
rubric.how: Name solar cooking or another application.

rubric.why: A third use completes the requested three applications.
rubric.description: Gives a third distinct use, such as electricity generation.
rubric.how: State that solar cells or panels generate electricity.

modelAnswer: Solar energy can be used to heat water.
It can be used to cook food in a solar cooker.
Solar cells can convert it into electricity.

written.text: Q10.1. Describe the harmful effects of the major pollutants present in the air.
written.finalAnswer: Air pollutants harm human health, plants and animals, reduce visibility, damage materials and contribute to smog, acid rain and climate change.

rubric.why: Health effects are a major consequence of air pollution.
rubric.description: Describes a health effect of a pollutant.
rubric.how: Mention poisonous CO or respiratory and other health harm.

rubric.why: Particles harm breathing and can reduce visibility.
rubric.description: Describes particulate-matter effects.
rubric.how: Mention lung harm or reduced visibility.

rubric.why: Sulphur and nitrogen oxides cause important environmental damage.
rubric.description: Links pollutant gases to acid rain or related harm.
rubric.how: Name the gases and the resulting acid rain.

rubric.why: Some pollutants alter Earth's heat balance.
rubric.description: Explains a climate-related effect.
rubric.how: Link greenhouse gases with warming or climate change.

rubric.why: The response should cover impacts beyond human health.
rubric.description: Mentions damage to living things, materials or air quality.
rubric.how: Give one further environmental effect.

modelAnswer: Carbon monoxide is poisonous and reduces the oxygen supply to body tissues; it can cause serious illness or death.
Particulate matter can enter the respiratory system, harm health and reduce visibility.
Sulphur and nitrogen oxides irritate the respiratory system and can form acid rain, which damages plants, soil and buildings.
Ground-level ozone and photochemical smog harm people and plants.
Greenhouse gases trap heat and contribute to global warming and climate change.

written.text: Q10.2. Explain greenhouse effect. How is global warming dangerous for us?
written.finalAnswer: Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing heat and keep some of it in the atmosphere. An increased greenhouse effect warms Earth and can cause climate change, melting ice, rising sea levels, extreme weather and harm to ecosystems and people.

rubric.why: The answer must identify gases involved in the effect.
rubric.description: Names greenhouse gases.
rubric.how: Give examples such as CO₂ or methane.

rubric.why: Absorption of outgoing radiation is the mechanism.
rubric.description: Explains that gases absorb outgoing heat radiation.
rubric.how: Describe the radiation absorbed.

rubric.why: Heat retention completes the explanation of the greenhouse effect.
rubric.description: Explains that heat is retained in the atmosphere.
rubric.how: Link absorption to heat being kept in the atmosphere.

rubric.why: The answer must explain the consequence of an enhanced effect.
rubric.description: Links increased greenhouse effect to warming or climate change.
rubric.how: State the temperature or climate consequence.

rubric.why: Specific dangers show how warming affects people and the environment.
rubric.description: Gives at least one danger of global warming.
rubric.how: Mention sea-level rise, weather, crops or ecosystem harm.

modelAnswer: Greenhouse gases such as CO₂ and methane absorb some of the outgoing infrared radiation from Earth.
They retain some of this heat in the atmosphere; this is the greenhouse effect.
An increase in greenhouse gases strengthens the effect and raises Earth's average temperature, causing global warming.
Global warming can change rainfall and weather patterns and increase extreme weather.
Melting ice and rising sea levels can threaten settlements, while changed climate can harm crops, ecosystems and human health.

written.text: Q10.3. What is air quality index? What information does it convey?
written.finalAnswer: The air quality index (AQI) is a scale or numerical indicator of air pollution; it communicates how clean or polluted the air is and the related health risk.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the index being defined.
rubric.description: Names AQI as an index or indicator.
rubric.how: Expand or use AQI.

rubric.why: An index expresses measured conditions in a usable form.
rubric.description: Describes AQI as a numerical scale or indicator.
rubric.how: State that it is a scale, number or indicator.

rubric.why: The index conveys the condition of the air.
rubric.description: States that AQI indicates whether air is clean or polluted.
rubric.how: Describe the air-quality information it gives.

rubric.why: AQI helps people understand possible health effects.
rubric.description: Mentions health risk or guidance for people.
rubric.how: State that it communicates health implications.

modelAnswer: The air quality index (AQI) is a numerical scale or indicator of air pollution.
It conveys how clean or polluted the air is.
It also indicates the possible health risk and helps people decide what precautions to take.

written.text: Q10.4. Who are high risk groups and why is pollution more dangerous for them?
written.finalAnswer: Children, older people and people with respiratory or heart disease are high risk groups because their bodies are more vulnerable to pollutants and they may suffer more severe effects.

rubric.why: Children are an explicitly vulnerable group.
rubric.description: Identifies children as a high-risk group.
rubric.how: Name children.

rubric.why: Other vulnerable groups should also be identified.
rubric.description: Names older people or people with existing illness.
rubric.how: Give at least one further high-risk group.

rubric.why: The answer must explain why these groups are affected more.
rubric.description: Explains increased susceptibility or reduced ability to cope.
rubric.how: Describe their greater sensitivity to pollution.

rubric.why: The explanation should connect vulnerability to real health harm.
rubric.description: States that pollution can cause more serious health effects.
rubric.how: Mention respiratory symptoms or severe illness.

modelAnswer: Children, aged people and people with respiratory or heart diseases are high risk groups.
Their bodies may be more vulnerable and less able to cope with polluted air.
Pollutants can worsen breathing and existing illness, causing more serious health effects.

written.text: Q10.5. Describe three strategies to address environmental issues.
written.finalAnswer: Use environmental education and public awareness, apply and enforce environmental laws, and adopt sustainable practices such as clean energy and reduced waste.

rubric.why: Education and awareness help people understand environmental problems.
rubric.description: Describes education or awareness as a strategy.
rubric.how: Explain how awareness encourages responsible action.

rubric.why: Rules and enforcement control harmful activities.
rubric.description: Describes environmental laws or their enforcement.
rubric.how: Mention standards, laws or monitoring.

rubric.why: Sustainable choices reduce pollution and resource damage.
rubric.description: Describes cleaner or sustainable practices.
rubric.how: Give a clean-energy or conservation measure.

rubric.why: A specific practical action makes the strategy concrete.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable action that reduces waste or pollution.
rubric.how: Mention reducing waste, recycling or controlling emissions.

rubric.why: The question specifically requests three strategies.
rubric.description: Clearly presents three distinct strategies.
rubric.how: Organise the response into three separate approaches.

modelAnswer: Environmental education and public awareness help people understand environmental issues and act responsibly.
Environmental laws, standards and their proper enforcement can control harmful emissions and activities.
Sustainable practices, including renewable energy, conservation, recycling and waste reduction, can lessen environmental damage.

written.text: Q10.1. Major Pakistani cities experience a very high AQI in winter which renders them the most polluted cities in the world. Point out some of the major causes of high AQI in these cities.
written.finalAnswer: Major causes include vehicle and industrial emissions, fuel and waste burning, construction and road dust, and winter weather that traps pollutants near the ground.

rubric.why: Vehicle emissions are a significant urban pollution source.
rubric.description: Names vehicle exhaust or traffic.
rubric.how: Identify emissions from transport.

rubric.why: Industrial emissions contribute pollutants to city air.
rubric.description: Names industrial or power-generation emissions.
rubric.how: Identify a major stationary source.

rubric.why: Burning fuels or waste releases pollutants and particles.
rubric.description: Names a burning source.
rubric.how: Mention fuel, waste or crop-residue burning.

rubric.why: Dust adds particulate matter to polluted air.
rubric.description: Names construction or road dust.
rubric.how: Identify a dust source.

rubric.why: Winter conditions can prevent pollutants from dispersing.
rubric.description: Explains how winter weather keeps pollution concentrated.
rubric.how: Mention stagnant air, inversion or reduced dispersion.

modelAnswer: Vehicle exhaust and heavy traffic release gases and particulate matter.
Industries and power generation add further emissions.
Burning fuels, waste and crop residues can increase smoke and particles.
Construction activity and road dust add particulate matter.
In winter, stagnant air and temperature inversion can trap pollutants close to the ground, raising the AQI.

written.text: Q10.2. Why does AQI not rise in Pakistan in hot days of summer?
written.finalAnswer: Strong heating makes air rise and helps pollutants disperse, while less smog-forming smoke may remain trapped near the ground; therefore AQI may not rise as it does in winter.

rubric.why: The answer must relate the effect to hot summer conditions.
rubric.description: Identifies strong summer heating.
rubric.how: Mention heating of the ground or air.

rubric.why: Rising air carries pollutants away from the surface layer.
rubric.description: Explains that heated air rises.
rubric.how: Describe upward movement of warm air.

rubric.why: Pollutant dispersal explains why near-ground air can improve.
rubric.description: Explains that pollutants disperse or mix into a larger volume of air.
rubric.how: Link rising air to better dispersal.

rubric.why: A contrast with winter trapping completes the explanation.
rubric.description: Connects improved dispersal with a lower AQI than during winter episodes.
rubric.how: Explain that pollution is less trapped near the ground.

modelAnswer: On hot summer days, the ground heats the air above it.
The warm air rises and carries pollutants upward, where they disperse and mix with a larger volume of air.
Unlike winter conditions, pollution is less likely to remain trapped close to the ground.
Therefore, AQI may not rise as it does during winter pollution episodes.

written.text: Q10.3. How has climate change affected Pakistan during the last five years?
written.finalAnswer: Pakistan has faced more severe heatwaves, irregular rainfall, floods and drought conditions, affecting people, agriculture, water resources and infrastructure.

rubric.why: Rising temperatures and heatwaves are important climate impacts.
rubric.description: Identifies severe heat or heatwaves.
rubric.how: Name a heat-related change.

rubric.why: Changing rainfall can cause damaging floods.
rubric.description: Identifies heavy rainfall, monsoon changes or floods.
rubric.how: Name a water-related impact.

rubric.why: Dry periods and rainfall irregularity are another impact.
rubric.description: Identifies drought, water shortage or irregular rain.
rubric.how: Name a dry or variable-rainfall impact.

rubric.why: The answer should show effects on people or economic activity.
rubric.description: Describes consequences for people, health, crops or livelihoods.
rubric.how: State a social or agricultural effect.

rubric.why: Consequences such as damage make the impact concrete.
rubric.description: Mentions damage, displacement or other serious loss.
rubric.how: Give one clear consequence of these events.

modelAnswer: In recent years, Pakistan has experienced severe heatwaves and unusually high temperatures.
Irregular and intense rainfall has contributed to damaging floods in some areas, while other areas face dry conditions and water shortages.
These events damage homes, roads and other infrastructure and affect people's health and livelihoods.
Agriculture and crops are also affected by heat, floods and changing water availability.

examTips: Section A tests facts and cause-and-effect links; read every option carefully, especially pairs such as sulphur and nitrogen oxides.
For short answers, give the direct fact first, then add one cause or effect if needed.
For constructed responses, show the link in order: pollutant or source → process → effect or control measure.
For descriptive questions, organise the answer into clear points and use relevant terms such as greenhouse effect, acid rain, AQI and particulate matter.
In investigative answers, connect local causes or weather conditions to the pollution level or climate impact.

steps.text: Solar energy can be used to heat water.

steps.text: It can be used to cook food in a solar cooker.

explain.title: Air pollutants and their sources
explain.body: Air pollution includes harmful gases and particulate matter. Vehicles, industries, fuel burning and dust can add pollutants to the air. Carbon monoxide is poisonous, while fine particles can harm the respiratory system.

explain.title: Greenhouse effect and global warming
explain.body: Some gases, including carbon dioxide and methane, absorb outgoing heat. More of these gases can strengthen the greenhouse effect and cause global warming and climate change.

explain.title: Acid rain and smog
explain.body: Sulphur and nitrogen oxides can contribute to acid rain. Photochemical smog forms when nitrogen dioxide and volatile organic compounds react in sunlight.

explain.title: AQI and people at risk
explain.body: The air quality index indicates how polluted air is and communicates health risk. Children, aged people and people with existing health problems are especially vulnerable.

explain.title: Reducing environmental harm
explain.body: Cleaner energy, efficient vehicles, controlled industrial emissions, less waste, environmental education and effective rules can all help reduce pollution.

mistakes: Do not confuse CO with CO₂: carbon monoxide is the more poisonous gas.
Do not say that all gases cause the greenhouse effect; the effect depends on whether a gas absorbs outgoing heat radiation.
Remember that both sulphur oxides and nitrogen oxides contribute to acid rain.
For AQI questions, explain both what the index indicates and why the reading changes.
For longer answers, give causes and effects rather than only listing pollutant names.
